classification.difficultyReason: Calculate rectangle areas and compare each with the original, recognising that changing both dimensions compounds their scale factors; the completed doubling row scaffolds the comparisons.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}A&=lw\\A&=4\times12\\A&=48\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$$ Compared with row a, the width is doubled and the length is unchanged, so the area doubles.
$$\begin{align*}A&=lw\\A&=8\times12\\A&=96\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$$ Compared with row a, both dimensions are doubled, so the area is multiplied by $2\times2=4$.
$$\begin{align*}A&=lw\\A&=2\times6\\A&=12\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$$ Compared with row a, the length is halved and the width is unchanged, so the area halves.
$$\begin{align*}A&=lw\\A&=4\times3\\A&=12\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$$ Compared with row a, the width is halved and the length is unchanged, so the area halves.
$$\begin{align*}A&=lw\\A&=2\times3\\A&=6\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$$ Compared with row a, both dimensions are halved, so the area is multiplied by $\frac12\times\frac12=\frac14$.
